# Blender Pipeline

## Principle

**Every runtime 3D asset in Magnet Rush is generated by script**, and every hero
asset is additionally *reviewed by eye* from the gameplay camera before it
ships. There is no manual modelling and no manual export step: the art source of
truth is Python, so assets are diffable, reviewable, reproducible on any
machine, and regenerable in one command. Editable `.blend` files are saved
alongside as `art/blender/src/`, but they are outputs of the scripts, not the
source of truth.

## Toolchain

Blender MCP **was connected and used** for this pass. It is now the primary
authoring workflow for hero assets, and the headless generator is the
reproducible fallback for bulk regeneration.

| | |
|---|---|
| Blender | 5.2.0 LTS |
| Blender Python | 3.13.13 |
| Interactive authoring | Blender MCP (`mr_hero.py`, `mr_env.py`) |
| Bulk regeneration | headless `--background` (`build_assets.py`) |
| Output | GLB (binary glTF 2.0) in `assets/models/` |

The reason to use MCP rather than only scripting: **assets can be rendered and
judged from the actual gameplay camera before export.** `mr_hero.setup_review()`
builds a portrait render with the same elevated three-quarter angle, cool key
light, blue rim and dark navy world the game uses, and renders it. The Kanban
Core went through five such reviews:

1. solid crystal + three near-coplanar rings — read as an ice rock with hoops
2. rings given genuinely different axes, emission cut so the blue stopped
   blowing out to white
3. shell split into two caps so the energy chamber could be seen at all
4. chamber changed from a buried sphere to a disc that fills the seam
5. seam plane tilted, because a level cut reads as a grin from an elevated
   camera

None of that is visible from a headless script. Each revision was a judgement
made on a rendered frame.

**Two hard rules learned in this session, both now enforced in code:**

* **Never wipe the file.** An interactive Blender session may hold unsaved work.
  `mr_hero` never calls `read_factory_settings`; it works inside a dedicated
  `MR_Build` scene and leaves every other scene alone. The unrelated 59-object
  project that was open throughout was never touched.
* **Never export with `use_selection`.** In an interactive session it also picks
  up what is selected in *other* scenes. Early Core exports silently welded a
  stray 480-triangle prop from that unrelated project into every file — 75% of
  each GLB. `mr_hero.emit()` now links the target object into a throwaway
  single-object scene and exports with `use_active_scene`, which cannot be
  contaminated by selection state anywhere.

Blender-only renders are **not** evidence the runtime looks right. Every asset
in this pass was also checked in a screenshot from the running Android build,
and several looked wrong there despite reviewing well in Blender — most notably
the Core, whose emission was tuned against an EEVEE preview and rendered as a
dull blue lump on device.

## Layout

```
art/blender/
  mr_kit.py         shared kit: palette, materials, primitives, export
  mr_hero.py        hero authoring: asymmetric crystals, split caps, crack
                    networks, mechanical rings, decks, greeble, circuits,
                    understructure, gameplay-camera review renders
  mr_env.py         the Level 1 platform kit, obstacles and set dressing
  build_assets.py   original headless generator (metal library)
  src/*.blend       editable sources, saved after each MCP session
assets/models/
  core/  metal/  platforms/  obstacles/
tool/
  asset_audit.py    parses every shipped GLB -> docs/asset_manifest.md
assets/models/
  core/  metal/  platforms/  obstacles/
```

## Commands

```sh
# everything
blender --background --python art/blender/build_assets.py

# one or more groups
blender --background --python art/blender/build_assets.py -- core metal

# refresh the human-readable manifest
python art/blender/write_manifest_md.py
```

The build **fails with a non-zero exit code if any asset exceeds its triangle
budget**, so the budgets in the brief are enforced by CI rather than by
convention.

## The kit (`mr_kit.py`)

**Palette.** The art bible's colour roles are constants (`CYAN`, `CORE_BLUE`,
`SILVER`, `CHARCOAL`, `ORANGE`, `GREEN`, …). Assets reference roles, never raw
values, so a palette change is one edit.

**Materials.** `material()` builds a Principled BSDF and caches it by name, so
repeated props share one material instance and the exported scene keeps its
material count low. The cache is cleared by `reset_scene()`, since reloading the
file frees every datablock.

**Primitives.** All low-poly by construction: `box`, `icosphere`, `cylinder`,
`cone`, `torus`, `gear`, `crystal`, `bevel_plate`. `crystal()` is the signature
one — an icosphere with per-vertex radial jitter, flat-shaded, which produces
the faceted energy-crystal silhouette the Kanban Core needs.

**Composition.** `join()` merges objects into a single mesh while remapping
material indices, so a multi-part prop still exports as one primitive per
material rather than a node hierarchy.

**Export.** `export_glb()` recalculates normals, applies transforms, exports the
selection as GLB, and returns a manifest record (triangles, materials, bytes).

## Conventions enforced in code

* metric scale, 1 unit = 1 metre
* transforms applied — every mesh exports at identity
* normals recalculated outward
* **flat shading everywhere** — the faceted look is the art direction, and it
  also lets the swarm batcher stamp templates without smoothing artefacts
* pivots at the logical centre of rotation
* **no textures at all** — flat colour plus emission. This keeps the APK small
  and sidesteps texture-compression format fragmentation (ETC2 vs ASTC vs BC)
  across Android GPUs entirely.

## Relationship to the swarm batcher

Swarm-class assets are not only loaded as GLB nodes. Their geometry is also
consumed as CPU-side templates by the batcher described in
`docs/renderer_decision.md`, which stamps them through per-object transforms
into a single merged mesh. That is why swarm pieces carry the tightest budget
(≤500 triangles, most are 12–44): those counts are multiplied by up to ~220
concurrent objects every frame.

## Current output

54 assets, 7,124 triangles, ~481 KB total, 0 budget violations. Full table in
`docs/asset_manifest.md`.

Verified end-to-end on an Android device build: `assets/models/core/kanban_core.glb`
loads via `Node.fromGlbAsset` and renders through Impeller, with the HUD
reporting `core: BLENDER GLB`.

## Remaining groups

The obstacle, enemy and boss libraries in sections 8–10 of the brief are not yet
generated. They extend `build_assets.py` with additional `build_*` functions and
a `GROUPS` entry — no new infrastructure is required. See
`docs/known_limitations.md`.
